articles.title: ‘Obvious weakness’: Zelenskyy slams Trump’s Russian diesel deal, warns it could prolong war
articles.body:
Zelenskyy calls Russia sanctions relief without de-escalation deal ‘obvious weakness’
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Friday (local time) warned that easing sanctions against Russia without a clear and lasting de-escalation agreement would be an “obvious weakness” that could prolong the war by allowing Moscow to continue selling petroleum products.In a post on X, Zelenskyy said peace could not be achieved through weakness and called for stronger sanctions, continued support for Ukraine and sustained pressure on Moscow to end the war.
"Peace never comes through weakness. Today, representatives of the US Congress were in Kyiv – a bipartisan delegation – and I am grateful to them for visiting Ukraine at such a difficult time. They asked: what is needed to end the war? The answer must be strong. There must be sanctions under the Lindsey Graham bill, there must be support for Ukraine in protecting lives, and there must be pressure on Russia for its war. And today, there was a conversation between the leaders of America and Russia. A conversation that leads to something different," he wrote.
Referring to the diesel announcement, Zelenskyy said, “Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world.
Russia will ‘repay’ the diesel with further terror and perfidy. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged.""Recently, there was a European decision to lift sanctions on Russian oligarchs. Since then, Russian strikes and the torment of people have only increased," he added.Citing recent Russian attacks across Ukraine, Zelenskyy said, "This past week alone, there was a brutal Russian missile strike on a residential building in Pryluky, aerial bombs were dropped on Kramatorsk – on ordinary city buses – and there have been constant attacks on Kyiv’s energy infrastructure and on the life-sustaining infrastructure in Dnipro, Kharkiv, Odesa, and our other cities. Dozens of people have been killed and hundreds wounded."He alleged that Russia was resorting to such attacks because it was struggling to achieve its objectives on the battlefield. "The Russians are compensating for their inability to achieve their objectives on the battlefield with this kind of terror. This year, Russia is weaker on the battlefield than at any other point in the war. That is why Putin is relying on terror. That is why he is relying on attempts to strike backroom deals to secure some form of pressure relief for Russia, in order to buy more time and more opportunities for war," he further said.Zelenskyy said Ukraine was prepared to take reciprocal steps towards de-escalation, adding that the American team was aware of Kyiv’s position."Ukraine is ready to take symmetrical de-escalatory steps, and the American team knows our position. Our strikes on Russian oil refineries and other oil facilities are a response to Russia’s years-long campaign of terror against Ukraine’s energy sector. Ukraine will not set Russian oil refineries on fire if Russia does not destroy our energy infrastructure. This is the kind of agreement we are proposing to America, and we believe the United States has enough power to achieve such a compromise," he said.
Zelenskyy’s remarks came after US President Donald Trump spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin and announced a deal to secure diesel supplies from Russia, marking a shift in Washington’s pressure on Moscow over the war in Ukraine as the US seeks to address rising fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections.In a social media post on Friday, Trump said Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel, followed by another 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”. He added that Russia would deliver another 3 million tonnes “within a short period of time”.The announcement came just a month after Trump signed a sweeping Russia sanctions law aimed at curbing Moscow’s oil and gas revenues, which help fund its war against Ukraine.

articles.title: Ukraine hit by deadly Russian strikes as ‘thanks’ for Trump diesel deal, Zelenskyy says
articles.body:
Russia launched deadly strikes on civilians in Ukraine as “thanks” for a deal cut by Donald Trump with Vladimir Putin to buy large quantities of Russian diesel, Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said, accusing Washington of helping fund Moscow’s war.
The Ukrainian president has expressed outrage at the agreement announced by Trump on Friday, which the US president said was needed to reduce diesel prices, and comes ahead of November’s midterm elections in which fuel costs are a key voter issue.
The deal, which appeared to blindside Kyiv as it was announced while Ukrainian negotiators were in Miami for peace talks, was described by Zelenskyy as a “gift” to Russia’s president.
He said Russia would use the money it raised from the fuel sales to invest in its war and that “any easing of sanctions” would play into Russia’s hands, “allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer”.
That prediction was realised hours later, when Ukrainian officials announced that a barrage of Russian strikes on the country’s south-east early on Saturday had killed 20 people, including three children.
“Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia,” Zelenskyy said on social media on Saturday.
“Last night confirmed once again that in Russia, they take any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they can keep dropping bombs on cities. Different signals are needed,” he said.
There were also “large-scale power outages” in the capital, Kyiv, the country’s largest private energy provider said.
Trump further stoked the fire on Saturday, saying it was time for Ukraine to get a new president, suggesting Zelenskyy has not done enough to end his country’s war with Russia and blaming him for high diesel prices in the US.
“I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal because he could have made many deals and for some reason he never does,” Trump said.
Andy Burnham reiterated his “complete solidarity” in a call with Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the leaders agreed to meet in person in the coming days to continue talks.
The prime minister said he recognised the past day had been “difficult for Ukraine” and the two talked about the importance of keeping up pressure on Russia, No 10 said.
In stark contrast to Zelenskyy’s open frustration with Trump, a Kremlin readout of Friday’s call between the US president and Putin was glowing, with the Russian news agency Interfax quoting an aide as saying it was “very substantive and friendly”.
“Neither wanted to be the first to hang up,” the Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said of the two leaders. “They hung up simultaneously, literally at the same time.” Zelenskyy has previously said Putin is playing games with Trump.
The diesel deal disrupts four years of western financial pressure on Moscow and leaves Kyiv’s allies in Europe and Nato scrambling to adapt their sanctions plan. The EU’s top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the diesel deal “provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war”.
“This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won’t,” she said on Saturday. “On Monday, EU foreign ministers intend to approve the biggest set of sanctions listings targeting Russia’s war machine since the start of the war.” She was referring to plans to formally add 1,600 new individuals and entities to the EU’s sanctions blacklist.
Major European governments have attempted to balance their diplomatic and trade relationships with a mercurial Trump and their support for Ukraine.
The German government spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said Berlin “remains committed to the sanctions imposed on Russia and is working with its European partners on further sanctions”, adding that support for Ukraine “remains unwavering”.
Ulf Kristersson, the Swedish prime minister, expressed “regret” at the US agreement, saying energy revenues were “a vital source of funding Russia’s war of aggression”.
Zelenskyy said on Saturday that Russia “must feel its losses” and has promised to respond. In the Russian-occupied Luhansk region, Ukrainian attacks in the past 24 hours had killed four civilians and wounded five, the region’s Russian-installed governor, Leonid Pasechnik, said on Saturday.
Zelenskyy said that Ukraine was ready to take “de-escalatory steps” in the war but only if Russia did the same.
Russia’s fuel production has become a key point of contention between Zelenskyy and Trump, who has attempted to stop Ukraine from bombing Russian refineries, which he says exacerbates a global diesel shortage. The Ukrainian leader has rejected such requests unless Russia stops attacking Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.
The Financial Times reported that during the talks in Miami, Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner raised the possibility that US intelligence sharing could be cut off if Kyiv did not halt the strikes.

articles.title: Child Killed, 2 Injured in Drone Strike Near Nikopol
articles.body:
An 11-year-old boy was killed and two other children were injured on Saturday, Oct. 10, when Russian forces dropped an explosive munition from an unmanned aerial vehicle in the Nikopol district of Dnipropetrovsk region, regional authorities reported.
Head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration Oleksandr Hanzha confirmed the casualties on his official Telegram channel, stating that the attack took place in the Pokrovska territorial community.

Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“An 11-year-old boy was killed as a result of an enemy attack in the Nikopol district,” Hanzha said. “The Russians dropped a munition from a drone in the Pokrovska community. Two more children were wounded – a 12-year-old boy and a 10-year-old girl.”
Hanzha stated that both surviving children were transported to a medical facility, where doctors are administering emergency medical assistance.
The Nikopol district, located across the Dnipro River from the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, faces daily Russian artillery shelling, loitering munition attacks, and tactical drone drops targeting civilian areas and municipal infrastructure.
Daylight drone and ballistic barrages across central Ukraine
The fatal drone drop in the Pokrovska community formed part of a wave of Russian strikes targeting non-combatants and civilian settlements across central and eastern Ukraine on Saturday.
In Kyiv, Russian forces conducted a daylight ballistic missile strike on the northern Obolonskyi district, hitting a restaurant building, sparking a major blaze, and scattering missile debris across an adjacent residential courtyard.
Major Drone Attack Paralyzes Moscow Airports, Flights Delayed
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko confirmed that the number of casualties from the capital’s restaurant strike rose to six, with five victims hospitalized and one treated on-site by emergency medical crews.
The ballistic barrage followed morning waves of turbojet loitering munitions that damaged electrical distribution nodes in Kyiv region, temporarily shutting down all three lines of the capital’s metro network, paralyzing electric surface transit, and cutting off municipal water supplies.
Climbing casualties in southern urban centers
Concurrently, emergency responders in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia continued recovering victims following a Russian guided aerial bomb (KAB) strike launched at 4:48 a.m. local time on Saturday.
The strike directly hit a five-story residential building and damaged 26 homes across the Shevchenkivskyi and Voznesenivskyi districts.
While initial morning assessments indicated four fatalities, the State Emergency Service and regional military authorities confirmed that the death toll surged to 17, including three children, as rescue brigades cleared collapsed masonry and searched for trapped residents beneath the rubble.
Another 16 civilians, including two children, sustained injuries.

articles.title: ‘Nuclear weapons not routine instruments of statecraft’: India’s warning to Pakistan at UN
articles.body:
‘India will not bow to nuclear blackmail’: New Delhi hits back at Pakistan at UN (Anmol Sher Singh Bedi)
NEW DELHI: India on Friday warned Pakistan against using nuclear weapons as a tool of political pressure, asserting that New Delhi would not bow to nuclear blackmail and that any terrorist attack against the country would invite a fitting response.Exercising its Right of Reply at the United Nations General Assembly's First Committee, which deals with disarmament and international security, India said nuclear weapons must not be treated as “routine instruments of statecraft”.Senior Adviser (Disarmament) at India's Permanent Mission to the Conference on Disarmament in Geneva, Anmol Sher Singh Bedi, delivered the response following remarks by Pakistan on Jammu and Kashmir.
“Jammu and Kashmir is an integral and inalienable part of India,” Bedi said, rejecting Pakistan's claims over the region.He said India's military capabilities were defensive in nature and shaped by its security environment, rather than directed against any particular country.“We heard concerns about escalation. These are legitimate concerns. However, these are best judged by conduct over time. Nuclear weapons must not be treated as routine instruments of statecraft,” Bedi said.
He warned that relying on the threat of nuclear weapons to shield activities below the threshold of conventional warfare could increase the risk of escalation rather than promote restraint.“A posture that relies on nuclear overhang to limit the consequences of subconventional activity raises the risk of escalation and not the prospect of restraint,” he said.Bedi also outlined what he described as a recurring pattern in regional crises, involving provocation, denial of responsibility and subsequent appeals for restraint after a response.“Where those in power are neither elected by people nor accountable to them, their decisions carry no risk and impose no cost for those who take them. That is how crisis becomes an instrument of power. That is how instability becomes useful, and that is how the cycle keeps on repeating,” he said.
India reiterates three red lines
India said its position on terrorism and national security remained clear, identifying three principles that would guide its response to threats.“First, any terrorist attack against India will receive a fitting response. Second, India will not bow to nuclear blackmail. Third, India will make no distinction between those who sponsor terrorism and those who mastermind it,” Bedi said.He said India's actions in May 2025 followed a “grave provocation” and were undertaken in self-defence after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir, in which 26 civilians, mostly tourists, were killed.“These actions were measured, targeted, and designed to be non-escalatory,” Bedi said.India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7, 2025, targeting what it described as terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir in retaliation for the Pahalgam attack. The Resistance Front, a proxy of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba, was linked to the attack.Bedi also stressed that the use of non-state actors by a country did not absolve it of responsibility for their actions.“The use of force by states under the garb of non-state actors does not erase the state's responsibility. India's right of self-defense remains intact,” he said.
India raises Indus Waters Treaty, nuclear proliferation
India also referred to the Indus Waters Treaty, arguing that the agreement depended on mutual trust and cooperation between the two countries.“A state cannot undermine those foundations of trust and cooperation and at the same time insist that the privileges flowing from the relationship remain untouched,” Bedi said.Following the Pahalgam attack, India announced that the treaty would be held in abeyance until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably ended its support for cross-border and other forms of terrorism.On nuclear proliferation, Bedi invoked the legacy of Pakistani nuclear scientist Abdul Qadeer Khan and the international proliferation network associated with him, which supplied nuclear equipment and expertise to countries seeking to develop nuclear weapons.
The network contributed to international concerns that led to United Nations Security Council Resolution 1540, adopted in 2004, which requires states to prevent the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their means of delivery to non-state actors.“This is relevant in the context of demands for unquestioned nuclear cooperation and transfer of advanced weapons and military capabilities. We urge all states and all responsible suppliers to exercise the highest degree of vigilance, not because of India, but for their own security,” Bedi said.
Ayush Pandey is a journalist at The Times of India, covering breaking news, politics, defence, and major legal and policy developments across India and the world. His reporting focuses on elections, national security, and institutional affairs, tracking the decisions and conflicts that shape public life. He specialises in sharp explainers and in-depth feature stories that go beyond headlines to decode political shifts, defence strategy, geopolitical flashpoints, and changing public sentiment. His work combines speed, clarity, and depth for a fast-moving digital audience.

articles.title: Trump strikes deal for over 4.8 million tons of Russian diesel despite sanctions
articles.body:
President Donald Trump announced Friday that he had reached an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin for more than 4.8 million tons of Russian diesel, a dramatic shift in U.S. policy toward Moscow as Washington seeks to ease soaring fuel prices ahead of the November midterm elections.
The announcement came just weeks after Trump signed sweeping sanctions legislation targeting Russia's energy sector over its war in Ukraine, raising questions about Washington's commitment to maintaining economic pressure on the Kremlin.
Trump said Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by another 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons shortly afterward. An additional 3 million tons would be delivered within a relatively short period, he said.
"Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority," Trump wrote on social media.
Shortly after the announcement, the U.S. Treasury Department issued a temporary license easing sanctions on Russian diesel exports. The authorization allows Russian diesel loaded onto tankers as of Friday to be supplied to global markets without triggering U.S. sanctions until April 2027.
The White House did not immediately clarify who would pay for the shipments, when the fuel would become available or whether deliveries scheduled for November would arrive before the November 3 elections.
The agreement comes as the war in Iran continues to disrupt global energy markets. According to AAA, the average price of diesel in the United States reached $6.23 per gallon Friday, after hitting a record $6.52 on September 22.
Zelensky: ‘Gifts to Putin will not bring peace’
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky sharply condemned the agreement, warning that increased Russian energy revenues would help Moscow finance its continued war against Ukraine.
"Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilised world," Zelensky wrote on X.
"Russia will 'repay' the diesel with further terror and perfidy. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged. What is needed is real de-escalation with Russia on a reciprocal basis," he added.
The Kremlin said the Trump-Putin phone call focused on prospects for resolving the war in Ukraine and also addressed developments in Iran.
Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev welcomed the agreement, saying cooperation between Moscow and Washington on diesel and energy would benefit the world.
The announcement also drew criticism from Democrats. Rep. Don Beyer, the senior House Democrat on the Joint Economic Committee, called the decision "infuriating" and accused Trump of undermining sanctions intended to weaken Russia's war economy.
The latest Treasury authorization follows several temporary exemptions granted to Russian energy shipments since the outbreak of the Iran war. However, it marks a more substantial relaxation of restrictions, extending beyond the shorter waivers previously issued.
For Moscow, the agreement offers an opportunity to expand energy revenues despite Western sanctions. For Kyiv, it represents a potentially damaging reversal of efforts to constrain Russia's ability to finance its invasion.

articles.title: Ukraine and Finland condemn Trump’s deal to import Russian diesel
articles.body:
Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo has condemned an agreement between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin to supply Russian diesel to American and global markets, describing the decision as a major disappointment.
Speaking to Finnish broadcaster Yle on Saturday, Orpo questioned whether the agreement would have any significant effect on fuel prices, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Washington of providing financial support to Russia during its war against Ukraine.
The agreement, announced by Trump on Friday, provides for Russia to deliver more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, followed by another 500,000 tonnes in November and one million tonnes thereafter.
Trump also announced plans for an additional three million tonnes, depending on the condition of Russian refineries damaged by Ukrainian attacks.
The US Treasury subsequently issued a temporary licence permitting imports of Russian diesel until 7 April 2027, easing sanctions introduced to restrict Moscow's energy revenues.
Orpo told Yle's Ykkösaamu programme that the announcement was a "terrible disappointment", although he stressed that the agreed quantities represented only a fraction of US diesel consumption.
He also questioned whether Russia would fulfil the deliveries and said he did not expect the agreement to have much impact on American or global markets.
Zelenskyy described the agreement as a gift to Putin and "an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged".
"Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world," Zelenskyy wrote on X, warning that Russia would repay the diesel with further attacks.
The announcement coincided with talks between Ukrainian, European and American representatives in Miami aimed at ending the war.
Trump defended the arrangement as necessary to reduce fuel costs following disruptions caused by the US-Israeli war against Iran, which began in February.
According to figures from the American Automobile Association reported by Reuters, average US diesel prices reached $6.28 per gallon on Thursday, approximately 70% above their level before the conflict.
Diesel prices have become a concern for the administration ahead of the 3 November congressional elections, particularly because of their effect on farming, transport and consumer costs.
The agreement also attracted criticism from American lawmakers. Republican congressman Don Bacon called for stronger sanctions against Russia rather than measures that would increase Moscow's revenues.
Energy specialists questioned the potential benefits for consumers.
In an interview with Finnish newspaper Ilta-Sanomat, Hanna Kalenoja, a transport specialist at the Finland Chamber of Commerce, said the agreement would primarily redirect existing Russian diesel exports rather than increase global supplies.
Russia has continued exporting diesel despite production disruptions caused by Ukrainian strikes on its refineries.
Kalenoja explained that the agreement would determine whether available Russian fuel reached the United States and its allies instead of Asian markets, where much of it has previously been sold.
She told IS that Finnish motorists were unlikely to see meaningful reductions in diesel prices as a result of the agreement.
Clayton Seigle, an energy strategist at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, also questioned the potential price benefits, telling the Associated Press that the agreement would provide Russia with additional export revenue without substantially reducing diesel costs in the United States or Europe.
Seigle said Russia was seeking buyers for its summer-grade diesel as domestic demand shifted towards winter and Arctic fuel grades.
Kalenoja identified Washington's willingness to ease sanctions on Russia in response to energy costs as a concern for Europe, where governments have maintained restrictions on Russian energy imports.
Meanwhile, the Finnish government continues discussing measures to help households and businesses facing higher fuel prices.
Orpo told Yle that proposals include tax changes, commuting deductions and support for professional drivers, but ministers have yet to agree on a package.
The prime minister also announced plans to propose ending tourist visas for Russian citizens across Europe at next week's European Council meeting, citing concerns about possible Russian sabotage operations.
HT

articles.title: Dozens reported injured in Yemeni Houthi attack at Riyadh airport
articles.body:
Yemen’s Houthis have launched a missile attack on Riyadh’s international airport in Saudi Arabia, with dozens reported wounded and a witness describing panic in the terminal.
Donald Trump told reporters he was evaluating whether the US should join Saudi strikes against the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen.
“We may. We’re going to look at it,” Trump said. “We just found out about the recent attack. So we’ll make a decision. We move very quickly.”
Saudi authorities did not confirm any new attack or evacuation, but one witness reported hearing an explosion while waiting to board a flight, and another said they saw a strike that left people wounded.
“I was on gate 403,” at the domestic terminal, the witness told Agence France-Presse. “I saw [gate] 401 hit, I saw injured [people] in front of my eyes. Everyone was running.”
A source at a local hospital told the news agency that five people were in intensive care after being wounded at the airport, and “dozens” more had been injured.
The relative of one injured person said they had been wounded in the shoulders and arms by shattered glass and taken to hospital.
Witnesses said people were being evacuated from the airport.
Saturday’s incident comes amid an escalation of missile strikes by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi on the kingdom. The airport has already been attacked twice this week, leaving four people dead and others wounded, and badly damaging an aircraft.
The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government unravelled in July.
The attack came as forces allied to the UN-recognised government in Yemen claim to have mounted a successful offensive to retake the Bab al-Mandab strait from Houthi rebels, but accounts vary as to whether the push has been repelled.
A Houthi spokesperson said forces from the Saudi-backed government based in Aden “were targeted with a large number of ballistic missiles, artillery support and heavy weapons, resulting in the destruction of more than 22 armoured vehicles and the killing and wounding of dozens, including a number of commanders.
“More than 30 ambulances arrived in Aden to transport the dead and wounded from the Saudi enemy’s mobilisations.”
By contrast, the Saudi ambassador to Yemen, Mohammed al-Jaber, said: “Blessed Friday and victory for every Yemeni and Arab. Bab al-Mandab has been cleared of the remnants of the Houthi terrorist militia.”
The exposed 5 sq mile (13 sq km) Perim Island straddles the strait, acting as a lookout point for all traffic from the Red Sea into the Gulf of Aden and towards the Indian Ocean. Aidarous al-Zubaidi, the president of the Southern Transitional Council (STC), one of the main political forces in the south of Yemen, claimed the island and coastal area had been recaptured from Houthi hands.
An official military spokesperson for the UN-recognised government forces qualified the claim, saying only half the area had been recaptured so far. Waddah al-Dabish said newly established Houthi defensive lines had been broken on the land next to the strait, leading to the death of thousands of Houthi fighters.
It is thought that as many as 500 Houthis fighters are stationed on the island, and Saudi Arabia is desperate to be able to report that the strait has been reclaimed to show that the land counteroffensive it launched at the beginning of the week is advancing.
The report came as the United Nations’ special envoy to Yemen, Hans Grundberg, admitted to the UN security council in New York that Yemen – the poorest country in the world – had lapsed back into full-scale war and said the first victims would be women and children.
The Houthis seized control of the strait two weeks ago and said no Saudi-linked commercial traffic would be permitted to go through the narrow waterway. The Houthis are waging a war to remove Saudi influence from Yemen, and have been mounting missile attacks on Riyadh in support of this objective.
There have been previous premature reports of military breakthroughs by the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since it launched its counteroffensive at the start of the week, but the recapture of the land by the strait and Perim Island (also known as Mayyun Island) is a military prize western governments desperately need.

articles.title: ‘Obvious weakness’: Zelenskyy criticizes Trump-Putin diesel deal over lack of de-escalation
articles.body:
Burç Eruygur
09 October 2026•Update: 09 October 2026
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Friday that easing sanctions on Russia without a de-escalation deal would be an "obvious weakness," following a diesel supply agreement announced by US President Donald Trump after talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
In a statement on US social media platform X, Zelenskyy said he had received a bipartisan delegation from the US Congress in Kyiv earlier Friday.
He said he called for stronger sanctions and increased pressure on Russia, as well as further support for Ukraine.
"And today, there was a conversation between the leaders of America and Russia. A conversation that leads to something different," Zelenskyy said.
The Ukrainian president argued that Russia's recent increase in airstrikes against Ukraine was intended to compensate for Moscow's "inability to achieve their objectives on the battlefield."
He accused Moscow of attempting to "strike backroom deals to secure some form of pressure relief for Russia, in order to buy more time and more opportunities for war."

"Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world. Russia will 'repay' the diesel with further terror and perfidy," Zelenskyy said.
"Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged. What is needed is real de-escalation with Russia on a reciprocal basis," he added.
Zelenskyy's remarks followed Trump's announcement of what he described as a "highly successful discussion" with Putin.
Trump said on his Truth Social platform that the talks resulted in an agreement for Russia to "immediately supply" more than 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to US and global markets.

articles.title: Putin Touts 90% Dollar-Free CIS Trade as Russia Sidesteps Western Sanctions
articles.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin used a summit of former Soviet republics in Turkmenistan on Friday, Oct. 9, to promote what Moscow sees as a financial lifeline against Western sanctions – claiming that 90% of Russia’s trade settlements with Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) countries now take place in national currencies rather than dollars or euros.
The announcement highlights how the Kremlin is using its post-Soviet economic networks to reduce reliance on Western financial systems while sustaining trade during its war against Ukraine.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
A $110 billion trade network beyond the dollar
Speaking at the summit in Avaza, a resort on Turkmenistan’s Caspian coast, Putin said Russian trade with CIS countries exceeded $110 billion in 2025 and continued growing in 2026.
He praised the development of a “stable financial infrastructure” independent of foreign influence, arguing that it allowed economic cooperation to continue despite outside pressure.
“It allows us to deepen economic cooperation regardless of foreign influence,” Putin said.
The shift toward national currencies has become increasingly important for Russia since Western governments imposed sweeping financial restrictions following Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Putin also urged CIS members to remove remaining obstacles to regional commerce.
“Barriers should be lifted,” he said.
How former Soviet trade routes help Russia evade sanctions
The risks extend beyond the currencies used to settle transactions.
Trump Says He and Putin Have Cut Diesel Deal, Zelensky Accuses Washington of ‘Weakness’
Western governments have repeatedly identified Central Asia and the South Caucasus as potential routes for restricted goods entering Russia through third countries.
The researchers identified two methods: rerouting sanctioned products through neighboring countries and misreporting the destinations of shipments passing through Russia.
They estimated that these channels offset roughly one-third of the decline in direct European exports to Russia in restricted product categories during 2022–23.
The goods involved included industrial equipment and dual-use products with potential military applications.
A shrinking club of former Soviet republics
The economic figures contrast with the steady erosion of the CIS’s political influence.
Established in December 1991 following the collapse of the Soviet Union, the organization was designed to preserve cooperation among newly independent republics.
Georgia formally withdrew in 2009 following Russia’s invasion the previous year.
Ukraine, one of the CIS’s founding states, gradually dismantled its participation after Russia’s annexation of Crimea in 2014 and accelerated its withdrawal from remaining agreements following the full-scale invasion in 2022.
Moldova has also moved toward a definitive break.
Armenia, meanwhile, has increasingly diversified its security and diplomatic relationships after years of dependence on Moscow.
Across Central Asia, governments are expanding economic cooperation with China, the European Union and Turkey while maintaining important commercial ties with Russia.
For Putin, however, the CIS remains a platform to demonstrate that Moscow retains regional influence despite its confrontation with Ukraine and the West.
Iran joins the gathering
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian attended the summit as a special guest, reflecting Moscow’s growing cooperation with another government facing extensive Western sanctions.
Putin and Pezeshkian met separately on Thursday, Oct. 8, discussing bilateral relations and the ongoing conflict involving Iran.
Pezeshkian thanked Moscow for opposing what he described as US unilateralism, while Putin offered Russian assistance in efforts to resolve the Middle East conflict.
Russia and Iran have expanded military and economic cooperation since Moscow invaded Ukraine, with Iranian-designed drones becoming an important part of Russia’s attacks.
The next CIS summit will take place in Bukhara, Uzbekistan, in October 2027, with Azerbaijan serving as co-chair before assuming the presidency and hosting the summit in 2028.
Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko welcomed Azerbaijan’s decision as a “historic moment” and expressed hope that Armenia would follow in 2029 – despite Yerevan’s growing distance from Moscow.

articles.title: China denies report of reciprocal nuclear site visits with US
articles.body:
Faisal Mahmud
09 October 2026•Update: 09 October 2026
China on Friday denied a report that Beijing and Washington had discussed reciprocal visits to nuclear facilities, with further talks reportedly planned in the coming months.
"The relevant report is not true," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told a regular news conference in Beijing, according to an official transcript of the briefing.
The denial came after CNN reported, citing sources familiar with the matter, that China and the US had discussed possible reciprocal visits to nuclear sites.
According to an earlier CNN report, preliminary discussions covered possible visits to US Department of Energy laboratories and corresponding Chinese research centers, alongside potential access to nuclear test sites.
The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), in its June report, estimated that China possessed 620 nuclear warheads as of January 2026, compared with more than 5,000 held by the US, including retired warheads.
According to SIPRI, the world's nine nuclear-armed nations possessed an estimated 12,187 warheads, including 190 held by India, 170 by Pakistan, 90 by Israel and 60 by North Korea. Russia and the US together accounted for nearly 86% of the global inventory.
SIPRI said China was expanding its nuclear arsenal faster than any other country, while Washington and Moscow continued extensive nuclear modernization programs.
The developments follow the expiration of the New START nuclear arms reduction treaty between Washington and Moscow in February.

articles.title: Trump announces Russian diesel deal amid soaring US fuel prices
articles.body:
Trump announces Russian diesel deal amid soaring US fuel prices
Russia to supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, followed by 1.5 million more, as prices soar amid the Iran war.
United States President Donald Trump said that Russia has agreed to supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel fuel to global markets amid discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
“I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the American and global marketplace, another 500,000 tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 tons immediately thereafter,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform.
The president added that Russia would deliver an additional 3 million tonnes of fuel “within a short period of time”. He said that the country would supply 500,000 tonnes in November.
An envoy for Russian President Vladimir Putin, Kirill Dmitriev, praised cooperation between Russia and the United States on diesel and energy in a post on X shortly after.
“Russia-US cooperation on diesel and energy will benefit the world,” Dmitriev wrote on X.
Putin-Trump call
The Kremlin said Putin told Trump in a phone call on Friday that Russia was ready “to supply oil” to the US and world markets.
“The Russian side reaffirmed its readiness to supply oil and oil products to the American and world markets,” the Kremlin said regarding the talks.
The Kremlin said the call between Putin and Trump, which lasted an hour and half, covered large-scale economic initiatives, including Russian fuel supplies.
The read-out from Moscow said Trump welcomed Russia’s involvement in efforts to settle the war with Iran.
Earlier this week, Putin met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Turkmenistan and told him Russia would “do everything” to help end the war, Russian news agencies reported.
In a call on Wednesday, Putin told Pezeshkian that Moscow was prepared to mediate, according to Iran’s IRNA news agency.
Putin told Trump that Russia would consider when to resume peace talks, the Kremlin said. It added that both leaders were interested in taking part in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China in November.
Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Trump warmly congratulated Putin on his birthday during the call and wished him success and wellbeing.
Petrol price pressures
The deal comes despite Ukrainian air strikes, which have taken more than half of the country’s oil refining capacity offline, according to claims made by Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence on Sunday.
The latest announcement comes a week after the G7 countries agreed to release 100 million barrels amid pressure from the White House.
The move also comes as prices of diesel, used in agriculture, heating homes and trucking goods, are near record highs ahead of the November 3 congressional elections that will determine control of Congress.
Diesel prices have been elevated in recent months but have started to decline. The average price for a gallon is $6.27 ($1.66 per litre), according to the American Automobile Association (AAA), which tracks daily petrol prices. That’s down $0.10 from this time last week, but up $5.94 from this time one month ago.
Diesel prices, which can drive inflation, are up 70 percent since the US and Israel’s war on Iran began this year, despite two high-profile recent moves by Trump to boost supplies of the fuel: pressuring allies to release emergency reserves and expanding access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel, which is normally used for farm equipment.
The wars in Iran and Ukraine have triggered an unprecedented global fuel supply crunch.

'Unworthy of our partners'
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy immediately slammed the offer.
"It is certainly not honest, it is certainly unworthy of our partners, and it is, in my view, a weak decision," he told reporters.
He said this would mean "extra money for the Russian war" against Ukraine, adding that "it only fuels Putin and gives him the opportunity to wage an even more intense war."
He said the Ukrainian team meeting with Trump's envoys in Florida on Friday and Saturday had "simply served as a front" for this agreement with Moscow.
According to the Kremlin, Putin and Trump also discussed the "settlement of the Ukrainian crisis, the situation surrounding Iran, as well as various aspects of bilateral relations", during their call.
Shortly after Trump's call with Putin, the US Treasury Department said on X that its Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) was "immediately issuing a temporary general license to allow the supply of Russian diesel to the global market."
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28, prompting Tehran to respond with missile and drone attacks across the region and effectively close the Strait of Hormuz.
The conflict has continued for more than seven months, driving up global energy prices as commercial oil traffic through the strategic waterway has effectively halted.
The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June after Pakistan and Qatar mediated to halt hostilities and pave the way for negotiations.
Implementation of the agreement has since stalled amid disagreements, including over security and navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Wicker Rejects Territorial Concessions to End War in Ukraine
articles.body:
US Senator Roger Wicker, chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, said on Friday, Oct. 9, that he cannot envision an end to the war in Ukraine that involves Kyiv ceding sovereign territory seized by Russia.
Speaking at a press conference in Kyiv, the senior Republican lawmaker affirmed that Russian President Vladimir Putin will not succeed in defeating the Ukrainian people, even as Moscow seeks to weaponize the upcoming winter to break civilian resilience, Interfax-Ukraine reported.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“Vladimir Putin will not be able to defeat the Ukrainian people this year or next year. If we allow it, he can make the lives of Ukrainians miserable, and I think that is precisely what he wants,” Wicker told reporters, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine.
Wicker noted that Ukraine faces another challenging winter following severe Russian infrastructure bombardments over the past year. He warned that Russian forces are deliberately expanding targeting parameters beyond electricity and district heating networks to include water supply systems.
“We do not know how difficult the conditions will be, but the Russian dictator’s goal is to make people’s lives miserable,” Wicker said. “In addition to blackouts and the lack of heating and electricity, we understand that Vladimir Putin also aims to strike the water supply system to further compound people’s suffering.”
The senator stressed that while Ukrainians do not seek prolonged hardship, they remain determined to resist Russian aggression.
Putin Touts 90% Dollar-Free CIS Trade as Russia Sidesteps Western Sanctions
“Given the events of recent years and current circumstances, I do not see an end to the war that involves the Ukrainian people giving up their sovereign territory seized as a result of an invasion that violates international law,” Wicker said.
Trump diesel pact
Wicker’s rejection of territorial concessions coincides with growing scrutiny in Kyiv and European capitals over Washington’s diplomatic posture toward Moscow.
On Friday, Oct. 9, US-led peace talks held in Miami – bringing together US, Ukrainian, and European officials alongside representatives of Britain, France, Germany, the European Commission, and NATO – concluded after a single six-hour session without a announced breakthrough.
US special envoy Steve Witkoff characterized the discussions as constructive, noting that delegates examined avenues to de-escalate and conclude the conflict ahead of winter.
However, the Miami consultations were overshadowed by US President Donald Trump’s announcement of an agreement with Putin to permit Russian diesel shipments to American and global markets.
Trump confirmed that Russia would supply over 300,000 metric tons of diesel immediately, followed by another 500,000 tons in November, prompting the US Treasury Department to issue a temporary sanctions waiver.
President Volodymyr Zelensky and lawmakers from both parties in Washington criticized the transaction, warning that easing economic restrictions and purchasing Russian petroleum products provides fresh financial revenue for Moscow’s war apparatus while peace delegations were actively negotiating.

articles.title: Trump’s Russian diesel deal, which drew fury in Ukraine, is unlikely to lower prices, experts say
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump said on 9 October that he had agreed with Russian leader Vladimir Putin to bring Russian diesel to world markets to lower energy prices. However, energy analysts say the deal, which drew fury in Ukraine, is unlikely to lower diesel prices meaningfully, CNN reports.
Trump wrote on social media that Putin would “immediately supply” more than 300,000 tons of diesel, with another 500,000 tons in November. Together, those volumes would cover about a day and a half of US demand, according to the US Energy Information Administration.
Meanwhile, former head of the Center for Countering Disinformation Andrii Kovalenko says that US diesel consumption alone is about 16 million tons per month, and global consumption is roughly 120 million tons.
The US experts read the move as politics more than a market shift. Trump spoke in tons rather than barrels because the figure looks bigger to an ordinary observer, said Dan Pickering, founder of Pickering Energy Partners, calling it “more politics than a game changer.”
Doubts Russia can even deliver
Former US officials question whether Putin holds the diesel Trump described, as Ukrainian strikes strain Russia’s refineries. A former senior State Department official says it hardly matters whether the fuel arrives, because Putin “has already achieved the result he wants,” with Trump believing he has a pre-election card that could move markets.
Even if the fuel flows, it would be a temporary measure. Gregory Brew of Eurasia Group says that he suspects Putin expects Ukraine to halt its strikes on Russian refineries in return, and that he cannot imagine Zelenskyy agreeing.
A win for Putin without conditions
For Putin, the gain is plain, Kovalenko says: he pushes for sanctions relief and for no new US sanctions, all without any demand to end the war in Ukraine.
"Trump’s bet was more on the news itself, driving prices down somewhat, because, in reality, figures like these shouldn’t bring prices down," Kovalеnkо believes.
He adds that Trump will "make a big fuss about diesel ahead of the elections, nothing more," and that the average American is unlikely to feel any lasting effect.”
Earlier, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that allowing Russia to sell petroleum products abroad without securing a lasting de-escalation agreement would help finance Moscow's war against Ukraine.
He criticized the decision, calling it "a birthday gift for Putin," per Axios.
The next day after the announcement, Russia launched six bombs on Zaporizhzhia, killing 17 people.

articles.title: Major Saudi conferences to proceed despite deadly airport attack
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Major Saudi conferences to proceed despite deadly airport attack
The organisers of two major Saudi energy and investment conferences said their events will go ahead this month and reassured visitors on security, after missile attacks on Riyadh's airport left four people dead and an airliner heavily damaged this week.
The attacks led to widespread flight disruptions, with people taking land routes or circuitous alternative flights. The UK, France and Germany have warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh.
Riyadh is sticking to plans to convene global events and trying to draw in investment even amid escalating war with the Iran-backed Houthis in neighbouring Yemen that has seen the kingdom attacked dozens of times over the past weeks.
Organisers of the World Petroleum Congress, set to host top global oil executives and policymakers from Sunday to Thursday, said it would proceed as planned with foreign leaders and ministers in attendance, an email sent to delegates said.
"Your comfort is our priority," it said, noting that alternative routes to Riyadh, including via a four-hour drive from Dammam on the kingdom's eastern coast, were available.
Italian Energy Minister Gilberto Pichetto Fratin on Friday said he would not fly to Riyadh for the International Energy Forum Ministerial Meeting, an event on WPC's sidelines, but would participate via video link.
The Future Investment Initiative, launched by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman as the kingdom's flagship investment conference a decade ago, would also proceed as planned from 26-29 October, organisers said.
"Safety and well-being remain our highest priority," a statement attributed to FII CEO Maha Al Saud said.
"Comprehensive security measures will be in place at Riyadh's airports, our conference venues and official hotels, with coordinated arrangements for participants' transportation," it said.
Chief executives of some of the world's biggest financial institutions such as JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon and Citi's Jane Fraser were on the list of expected attendees. Citi and JPMorgan did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Houthis have said airliners should avoid Saudi airspace, declaring it a zone of military operations after the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an offensive against the group earlier this month.
Germany's Lufthansa has suspended Riyadh flights through 16 October while Gulf carriers Etihad Airways and Flydubai have cancelled flights to and from the Saudi capital scheduled for 10 October.
Saudi Arabia has responded to Houthi attacks with a wave of strikes on missile launcher sites, vowing to protect the kingdom, and says it has intercepted many ballistic missiles fired by the group.

articles.title: Zelenskyy: US used meeting with us to strike deal with Putin behind our backs
articles.body:
Zelenskyy: US used meeting with us to strike deal with Putin behind our backs
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused US President Donald Trump's team of acting dishonestly by inviting a Ukrainian delegation to talks in the United States before striking a deal with Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin behind its back to lift sanctions on Russian diesel.
Source: Zelenskyy in a telephone interview with Axios
Details: Zelenskyy said that a few days ago, US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff proposed a meeting in Florida to discuss new American ideas for ending the war. However, during talks between the Ukrainian delegation and Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the US side did not once suggest that it was considering a deal with Russia to purchase millions of tonnes of diesel fuel.
It was only an hour before Trump's official announcement that the Ukrainian negotiators were informed that the US president planned to speak to Putin and lift sanctions. Zelenskyy stressed that this was unfair to Ukraine.
Quote: "Steve proposed to meet in Florida. And of course I accepted to go there and speak about the possibilities of negotiations. The Americans said they have some ideas and we agreed to come to discuss.
It's not honest, really, because we tried to build our relations in the best way. It looks like that they used this opportunity to meet us from one side, and from the other side called Putin and negotiate this."
Details: Zelenskyy stressed that he would support easing energy sanctions only in exchange for an energy ceasefire. Instead, he said, the current situation demonstrated US weakness, as Washington had secured no concessions in return.
Quote: "What did [Trump] get? That he will have more diesel? For whom? More Russian diesel for Americans? It shows weakness of the world. It looks like Alaska No. 2.
You know, it looks like a happy birthday present for Putin. It looks absolutely terrible."
Details: Zelenskyy also suggested that Trump's representatives were trying to secure another visit to Moscow through the agreement.
Quote: "If you allow them to export diesel, and you think before that you have to go to Russia to negotiate, it looks that you are buying this meeting. Maybe I'm not right. But it looks this way. Otherwise, why do it?"
Details: Zelenskyy said he plans to obtain a full briefing from the Ukrainian negotiating team to establish whether the agreement is connected to the planned visit to Russia by Trump's envoys.
Despite his anger, Zelenskyy refrained from stating that Ukraine would reject US mediation. He stressed that "we need the Americans to try to stop this war".
Background:
- On the evening of 9 October, Trump said he had spoken by phone with Putin and agreed on supplies of millions of tonnes of Russian diesel to US and global markets.
- The US Department of the Treasury, through its Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), issued General Licence No. 135, authorising transactions involving the sale, delivery, unloading and import of Russian-origin diesel fuel into the US until 17 April 2027.
- Zelenskyy strongly criticised Trump's actions, describing the easing of sanctions as an "absolutely terrible" move. He stressed that this "happy birthday present for Putin" will provide Russia with billions more to continue the war.
- Zelenskyy said Ukraine's negotiating team in the US was being used as "cover" while Trump and Putin reached agreements on fuel supplies.
- Following his conversation with Trump, Putin confirmed that Russia is ready to supply petroleum products to the US and global markets. He also expressed hope for continued cooperation between the two countries.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia says three killed at airport as Yemen war expands
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Saudi Arabia says three killed at airport as Yemen war expands
Saudi Arabia said on Friday that three people including a pilot were killed in attacks on Riyadh international airport the day before when Yemen's Houthis claimed hits on the facility.
Houthi media reported on Friday that Saudi attacks on Sanaa airport killed two people, while the civil defence agency in the Yemeni capital reported extinguishing fires caused by Saudi strikes, including one that it said destroyed a factory.
The conflict between the Iran-backed Houthis and Yemen's internationally recognised government -- supported by Saudi Arabia -- surged in July, and has since spilled over into the neighbouring kingdom.
In addition to seizing territory along the Red Sea coast in Yemen, the Houthis have attacked transport hubs, oil facilities and other civilian targets in the world's largest crude exporter with drones and missiles.
The Saudi civil aviation authority said two attacks on Thursday on Riyadh airport and a Saudia airlines plane had "resulted in the martyrdom of three citizens".
The national carrier confirmed the death of the aircraft's captain.
The attacks on the Saudi capital forced diplomats stationed there to shelter in place and international schools to take safety measures, as explosions echoed across the city on Thursday.
Numerous flights at Riyadh airport were delayed or cancelled, and the civil defence agency said missile "interception debris" had damaged a kindergarten and a medical complex in the city.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree on Friday appeared to suggest that planes would need to seek the group's permission to fly in or out of Riyadh.
"Humanitarian flights to and from Riyadh Airport will be permitted for all flights authorised" by a Houthi coordinating body in Sanaa, he wrote on X.
'Advances are limited'
Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government forces it supports have struggled to reverse the Houthis' advance, despite a counter-offensive aimed at recapturing territory including the area around the Bab al-Mandab strait, which is crucial to global shipping.
While a Saudi diplomat said on Friday that Saudi-backed forces had retaken the area, a military source on the ground gave a conflicting account, saying fighting was ongoing.
The Yemeni military source told AFP that government forces had launched a "major operation" in the strait region, supported by Saudi air power, but added that "fighting is fierce and advances are limited".
Houthi-affiliated media, meanwhile, said an attack by government forces south of the strait had been repelled.
A regional source told AFP on Friday that Saudi Arabia would not bow to the Houthis' "military blackmail" and would not agree to a truce until the Yemeni government regained all the territory it lost in recent weeks.
The Houthis' Al-Massirah TV channel reported fresh Saudi strikes on Sanaa, shortly after a large demonstration in support of the group in the city.
The raids targeted military positions far from residential neighbourhoods, according to an AFP correspondent.
The Houthis, whose heartlands are among the Zaidi Shia Muslims in the northwest, had already controlled the capital Sanaa and most of Yemen's major population centres since the start of the war in 2014.
Riyadh's military coalition intervened to support the government the following year.
Evacuation warning
After declaring the start of their counter-offensive against the Houthis, Yemen's government claimed to have pushed the fighters out of strategic areas on the Red Sea coast and the port city of Mocha.
But the Houthis insist they are holding their territory, and military sources from both sides contacted by AFP have not reported any major changes on the ground.
The Houthis have warned workers to evacuate Saudi Arabia's oil facilities, having days before hit a major refinery south of the capital.
Admissions by Saudi authorities of civilian targets being hit are relatively rare. There have been few statements on Houthi attacks in recent weeks.
Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast and access for journalists difficult.
In Yemen, one of the world's poorest countries, ordinary civilians are paying the price for the renewed fighting, with more than 200,000 people displaced since July, according to UN data.

articles.title: US eases Russian diesel sanctions after Trump-Putin deal
articles.body:
The United States has temporarily eased sanctions on Russian diesel after President Donald Trump announced a supply agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin, drawing criticism from Ukraine that the move would help Moscow prolong the war.
The Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control issued a license on Oct. 9 authorizing the sale, delivery and import of Russian diesel, including shipments to the United States, until April 7, 2027.
Trump said on Truth Social that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tons to U.S. and global markets, followed by another 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons immediately afterward.
A further 3 million tons would follow, depending on the condition of Russian refineries, he said.
Trump predicted the supplies would bring down diesel prices, saying relief for American farmers, ranchers and truckers was a priority.
Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Moscow would immediately begin lifting its own diesel export restrictions ahead of schedule.
He told TASS that exports could reach 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons in December, potentially rising to nearly 3 million tons a month later.
Putin separately confirmed Russia’s readiness to supply oil and petroleum products to U.S. and global markets, saying the shipments would benefit the world economy.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized the agreement, arguing that easing sanctions without a clear and lasting agreement to reduce hostilities would give Russia more resources to continue fighting.
“Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged,” he wrote on social media.
Zelensky said Ukraine’s strikes on Russian refineries were a response to attacks on its energy infrastructure. Kiev was ready to halt those strikes if Moscow stopped targeting Ukrainian energy facilities, he said, urging Washington to broker a reciprocal agreement.
Asked about Zelensky’s criticism before departing the White House, Trump said the United States remained a strong partner of Ukraine. He also thanked Putin for the diesel agreement.

articles.title: 32-Element CRPA Antenna, Likely Manufactured in Alabuga, Was Found in Downed Geran-4 Drone
articles.body:
A 32-element CRPA antenna, likely manufactured at a plant in Alabuzha, Russia, was found in a Russian Geran-4 strike drone shot down in Ukraine.
This was reported by The Insider, citing an analysis of photos and videos of the downed drones.
The new antenna looks very similar to products made by the Chinese company Harxon, but shows signs of local production.
The rough finish of the metal casing and the factory marking ALB stamped directly onto it point to the possibility that production was localized in Russia.
The Russians are likely gradually transitioning to at least screwdriver-style assembly of such circuit boards in Tatarstan.
They first purchase test batches on marketplaces, and then order large production runs or license their manufacture.
Last year, it was revealed that the main supplier of multi-element antennas to Alabuga was the Chinese company Harxon. After this information was made public, the company fell under international sanctions, and its representatives announced the dismissal of employees who had been in contact with Russia.
As a reminder, it first came to light in July that Ukraine had seized a 32-element CRPA antenna that was mounted on a Russian weapon system.
This is effectively two antennas, each with 16 elements, assembled into a single unit. The first 16 elements operate in the L1 band, like the Kometa, while the other 16 operate in the L2 band. The L1 band operates at a base frequency of approximately 1,575 MHz and is the primary channel for civilian and military satellite navigation.
CRPA antennas, which support only the L1 band, are the most compact and inexpensive, which is why they are widely installed on drones and missiles. The L2 band operates at a lower frequency of approximately 1,227 MHz and is designed for transmitting secure and encrypted signals.
A CRPA antenna (Controlled Radiation Pattern Antenna) is a specialized navigation module designed to protect GPS/GLONASS satellite signals from electronic jamming. It consists of several separate antenna elements and a digital processor that analyze the surrounding space.
The number of elements in the antenna directly determines its resistance to interference. Each additional element allows the system to block yet another separate source of jamming.

articles.title: Major Drone Attack Paralyzes Moscow Airports, Flights Delayed
articles.body:
A major wave of Ukrainian strike drones targeted the Moscow region early Saturday morning, Oct. 10, prompting severe aviation restrictions that delayed or canceled hundreds of commercial flights across the Russian capital’s major international airports.
Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin claimed that Russian air defenses intercepted 403 unmanned aerial vehicles directed toward the capital region between 8:30 p.m. local time on Friday and 8:30 a.m. on Saturday.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Sobyanin stated that the vast majority of incoming drones were neutralized on distant approaches to the capital, while 25 were shot down within the immediate airspace approaching Moscow.
Russian monitoring networks and Ukrainian observers described the overnight assault as one of the largest coordinated drone operations directed against the Russian capital since the start of the full-scale war.
The drone barrage triggered temporary ground stops and flight restrictions across Moscow’s primary civil aviation hubs, with the most severe disruptions recorded at Vnukovo and Sheremetyevo, alongside secondary delays at Domodedovo.
Russia’s federal air transport agency, Rosaviatsiya, confirmed that flight suspensions were lifted at 8:50 a.m. local time, though airlines continued adjusting schedules throughout Saturday morning to clear mounting flight backlogs.
Estimates regarding the scale of the disruption varied across civil aviation tracking monitors.
Yabloko Leader Fined Over Anti-War Slogans on Duma Ballots
Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+ reported that approximately 300 scheduled commercial flights experienced cancellations or prolonged delays, while Russian regional news outlet MSK1 reported that at least 370 flights were delayed across the metropolitan airport cluster.
Systematic pressure on Moscow’s air corridors
The disruption across Moscow’s civil aviation network reflects an expanding Ukrainian operational campaign designed to degrade Russian rear logistics, overwhelm metropolitan air defense coverage, and impose tangible economic costs on the Russian heartland.
By forcing civil aviation authorities to repeatedly activate emergency air closure protocols – designated in Russian aviation procedures as the “Kover” (Carpet) plan – recurrent drone incursions disrupt commercial passenger operations, divert long-haul freight traffic, and strain radar tracking architectures deployed around the Russian capital.
The overnight strikes on the capital region coincide with wider Ukrainian precision strikes targeting Russian strategic logistical nodes and fuel infrastructure.
Overnight into Saturday, Ukrainian strike drones struck the Yug Rusi oil transshipment terminal in Rostov-on-Don, igniting a major fire at an export and military supply hub handling 2.5 million metric tons of petroleum products annually.
Consecutive strikes on Russian tech and data infrastructure
The overnight assault on Moscow follows consecutive Ukrainian drone strikes targeting foundational Russian digital and communications infrastructure in adjacent regions.
On Friday, Oct. 9, Ukrainian strike drones damaged a major data center belonging to Russian technology corporation Yandex in the regional capital of Kaluga, located southwest of Moscow.
Yandex confirmed that several hardware modules were completely disabled, warning users that disruptions to its search, ride-hailing, cloud storage, and corporate digital ecosystems could occur while technical teams assess physical damage.
Kaluga Regional Governor Vladislav Shapsha reported that the Oct. 9 drone waves injured nine people across the province, with five hospitalized following impacts in residential and industrial zones.
The Kaluga strike marked the second consecutive day of precision attacks targeting Yandex’s server infrastructure. On Thursday, Oct. 8, Ukrainian drones hit another Yandex data center situated in Sasovo within the Ryazan region, forcing a complete operational shutdown of the installation.
The resulting server outage produced cascading disruptions across major corporate networks and public services dependent on Yandex cloud hosting, including booking systems operated by Russian Railways (RZhD), mobile network operator MegaFon, and several national media organizations.
The compounding infrastructure damage prompted Yandex shares to drop roughly 4 percent on the Moscow Exchange.

articles.title: Japan Ordered Ukrainian Interceptor Drones From SkyFall
articles.body:
The Japan Ministry of Defense has signed a contract to purchase interceptor drones from the Ukrainian company SkyFall.

He noted that the ministry is currently working to ensure their delivery as soon as possible.
“The Japan Ministry of Defense has already signed a contract to purchase interceptor drones from the Ukrainian company SkyFall. We are currently working to ensure their delivery as soon as possible,” the official said during a briefing.

According to him, thanks to a rapid feedback cycle, new versions of drones with improved performance are released every two to three weeks.
The minister emphasized that Japan has much to learn from Ukraine in the areas of defense industry development and strengthening the industrial base. Read more about the topic in the article “Prospects for Japan’s Defense Industry and Its Cooperation With Ukraine.”
As Militarnyi previously reported, the Canadian company Calian Group and the Ukrainian company SkyFall announced a strategic partnership last month in the field of unmanned systems training. The collaboration aims to develop the training and operational readiness of the armed forces of Canada, NATO countries, and other allies.

articles.title: Russia Strikes Dnipropetrovsk Region Nearly 40 Times, Killing 1 and Setting Warehouses Ablaze
articles.body:
Russian forces struck the Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 40 times on Friday, Oct. 9, killing one person.
Head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration Oleksandr Hanzha reported the attacks in a series of updates. Russia used drones, artillery and a missile against communities in the Kryvyi Rih, Nikopol and Synelnykove districts throughout the day, before striking a logistics company’s warehouses near Dnipro twice.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
One person was killed in the Synelnykove district. However, local authorities did not provide further details about the victim at the time of the report.
Kryvyi Rih district
Kryvyi Rih, President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown and a major industrial center, repeatedly faces Russian missile and drone attacks.
The latest strikes damaged infrastructure in the city, while the nearby Zelenodolsk community suffered damages on private houses.
On Tuesday, Oct. 6, Russian forces attacked central Kryvyi Rih with two Banderol loitering munitions, striking the grounds of a city hospital and wounding three people.
Russian forces launched an overnight Russian barrage on Kryvyi Rih on Sept. 11-12, killing two people and wounding three. The strikes also damaged an industrial facility and civilian infrastructure, including private homes.
In August, a Russian strike on a shopping center in the city killed at least 16 people and wounded more than 130, including several children.
Among the deadliest strikes in the Kryvyi Rih was recorded on July 30, when Russian forces launched a missile on the village of Radushne, killing an entire family of 10, including two parents, seven children, and an 18-month-old grandson.
US Congress Delegation Backs Expanded Starlink Access for Ukraine
Nikopol and Synelnykove district
The Nikopol district bore the brunt of today’s strikes as Russian forces struck the city of Nikopol along with the Pokrovske, Marhanets, Myrove, Mozolevska and Chervonohryhorivka communities.
According to Hanzha, the strikes damaged private homes and an apartment building, as well as businesses and an infrastructure facility. Several fires were sparked.
Russian attacks targeted the Zaitseve and Petropavlivka communities in the Synelnykove district, damaging an agricultural enterprise and infrastructure facilities.
Double strike on Dnipro district warehouses
Later in the evening, Russian forces struck the Dnipro district, setting a logistics company’s warehouses on fire, Hanzha reported at 8 p.m. local time.
The company’s name had not been made public at the time of reporting.
Less than an hour later, at 8:50 p.m. local time, Hanzha confirmed the same warehouses were struck for a second time. Authorities are still determining whether anyone had been hurt.

articles.title: Trump says Russia to 'immediately supply' 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to US, global markets
articles.body:
Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the US and other global markets, US President Donald Trump announced in a Truth Social post on Friday.
Another 500,000 are expected to be supplied in November, and another 1,000,000 “immediately thereafter,” according to Trump.
“Between our TOTAL CONTROL of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!” Trump wrote in the post.
The announcement came following a "highly successful" discussion with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Putin's envoy praises US-Russian cooperation on diesel, energy after call with Trump
Russian President Vladimir Putin's envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, praised cooperation between Russia and the United States on diesel and energy in a post on X/Twitter on Friday, shortly after Putin spoke by phone with US President Donald Trump.
After Putin and Trump spoke, the US leader said Russia agreed to immediately supply over 300,000 metric tons of diesel fuel to the American and global market.
"Russia-US cooperation on diesel and energy will benefit the world," Dmitriev wrote on X.
Zelensky responded, calling the decision an 'investment in war'
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized an accord on Friday between the US and Russia allowing Moscow to provide the US with diesel as "an investment in a war that must be ended."
"Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world," Zelenskiy wrote on the X social media platform.
"Russia will 'repay' the diesel with further terror and perfidy. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged. What is needed is real de-escalation with Russia on a reciprocal basis," Zelenskiy said.
UK responds to the US-Russia diesel deal
The United Kingdom remains committed to supporting Ukraine and will maintain pressure on Russia through sanctions, a government spokesperson said on Friday, after US President Donald Trump announced a deal for Russia to supply diesel to the US and the global market.
"The UK's position could not be clearer. We will continue working closely with international partners to ensure Ukraine has the military and financial support it needs to defend itself. We will also maintain pressure on Russia through the toughest sanctions regime ever imposed by the UK," the spokesperson said.

articles.title: Zelensky: Letting Russia sell fuel means investing in its war
articles.body:
Zelensky: Letting Russia sell fuel means investing in its war
President Volodymyr Zelensky said this in a Telegram post, Ukrinform reports.
“Peace never comes through weakness. Today, representatives of the U.S. Congress were in Kyiv – a bipartisan delegation – and I am grateful to them for visiting Ukraine at such a difficult time. They asked: what is needed to end the war? The answer must be strong. There must be sanctions under the Lindsey Graham bill, there must be support for Ukraine in protecting lives, and there must be pressure on Russia for its war. And today, there was a conversation between the leaders of America and Russia. A conversation that leads to something different,” Volodymyr Zelensky said.
According to him, following the European decision to lift sanctions on Russian oligarchs, Russian strikes and abuses against civilians have only increased. Just this week, there was a brutal Russian missile strike on a residential building in Pryluky, airstrikes on Kramatorsk – targeting ordinary city buses – and continued attacks on Kyiv’s energy infrastructure and critical infrastructure in Dnipro, Kharkiv, Odesa and other Ukrainian cities. Dozens of people have been killed and hundreds injured.
“The Russians are compensating for their inability to achieve their objectives on the battlefield with this kind of terror. This year, Russia is weaker on the battlefield than at any other point in the war. That is why Putin is relying on terror. That is why he is relying on attempts to strike backroom deals to secure some form of pressure relief for Russia, in order to buy more time and more opportunities for war,” the President stressed.
Volodymyr Zelensky believes that gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world.
“Russia will ‘repay’ the diesel with further terror and perfidy. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged. What is needed is real de-escalation with Russia on a reciprocal basis,” the post said.
As Ukrinform reported, with U.S. approval, Russia will supply 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the global market and substantially increase its exports going forward.
